key_insight: RiVER shows that LLMs can be improved on coding tasks without ground-truth solutions by using calibrated, score-based reinforcement learning from deterministic execution feedback.
engineering_relevance: This makes reinforcement learning feasible for real-world optimization problems where only measurable performance scores are available, not exact labels.
method: Train on score-based tasks using deterministic execution feedback as continuous rewards.
Apply calibrated reward shaping to reduce scale dominance and frequency dominance.
Use instance-wise comparisons and emphasize top-ranked solutions while keeping bounded rewards for other valid outputs.
evidence_signal: The authors trained on 12 AtCoder Heuristic Contest tasks and reported gains on ALE-Bench, LiveCodeBench, and USACO, including +8.9% and +9.4% ALE rating rank for Qwen3-8B and GLM-Z1-9B-0414.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful reward calibration; raw execution scores can improve in-domain ranking yet fail to transfer to exact-solution benchmarks.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning without Ground-Truth Solutions can Improve LLMs
